result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give good, paste-ready token scales with suitable body, heading, code and caption values, and both shrink the h1 to roughly 70–75% on mobile. The deciding difference is line length: A caps the prose at 65ch, while B never limits the article column width at all. B does add useful extras (font stacks, colors, a pull-quote class), but none of them make up for the missing column limit. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give pasteable rem-based custom properties with good body, heading, code and caption values, and both scale the h1 from 40px down to about 70–75% on mobile. The deciding gap is the article measure: B caps prose at 65ch, while A sets no max-width at all, so A misses rubric item 2. B also adds useful refinements such as text-wrap and a smaller size for inline code, though A is more complete on font families and colors.
